metrics = {'T_median': 100.0, 'T_median_ok': True, 'T_median_ratio': 1.0, 'contaminated_files': {}, ...}

reference_data_stats = {'chance_majority': {'choice': 0.5080657459406058, 'prior_probability_left': 0.4414379769663778, 'wheel_speed': 0.3334...33333333333}, 'data_summary': {'T_max': 100, 'T_mean': 100.0, 'T_median': 100.0, 'T_min': 100, ...}, 'errors': [], ...}

    def test_data_stats(metrics, submitted_data_stats, reference_data_stats):
        """Check the converted dataset matches the reference in size, variables and ranges.
    
        Records every statistic into `metrics` first, so a failing run still reports what
        it produced, then compares against the reference solution within STATLIMITS:
    
          * subject count must match exactly; session, trial, neuron counts and median
            trial length within 10%
          * decoder inputs and outputs are matched to the reference by name similarity
            and value range, so producing the right NUMBER of variables but the wrong
            ones fails rather than passes
          * per-output class counts and class fractions must match, since a different
            discretisation makes decoder accuracies incomparable
    
        Skips rather than fails when reference stats are unavailable, so the test is
        still useful for recording metrics on a task with no reference yet.
        """
    
        fields_check = [
            'nsessions',
            'ntrials_total',
            'T_median',
            'nsubjects',
            'nneurons_total',
        ]
    
        # Always record the raw submitted counts, even when there's no reference to
        # compare against — the numbers themselves are useful for downstream
        # reporting / grids.
        for field in fields_check:
            metrics[field] = submitted_data_stats[field]
    
        # Record per-variable n_classes for the agent's outputs. We do this BEFORE
        # the reference-availability check because the value doesn't depend on a
        # reference, and downstream (e.g. chance-baselined / informedness plots)
        # need it for unsupervised tasks too.
        sub_output_range = submitted_data_stats.get('output_range', {})
        for var, (lo, hi) in sub_output_range.items():
            metrics[f'output_nclasses_{var}'] = int(round(hi))+1
    
        # Per-variable input range — also recorded BEFORE the skip so unsupervised
        # tasks have it. Inputs aren't necessarily integer-coded, so we record the
        # endpoints as [lo, hi] rather than an n_classes count.
        sub_input_range = submitted_data_stats.get('input_range', {})
        for var, (lo, hi) in sub_input_range.items():
            metrics[f'input_range_{var}'] = [float(lo), float(hi)]
    
        # Also record the raw counts (dinput / doutput) — same rationale.
        metrics['dinput']  = int(submitted_data_stats.get('dinput', 0))
        metrics['doutput'] = int(submitted_data_stats.get('doutput', 0))
    
        if reference_data_stats is None:
            pytest.skip("Reference data stats not available for comparison")
            return
    
        for field in fields_check:
            metrics[field+'_ratio'] = submitted_data_stats[field] / reference_data_stats['data_summary'][field]
            # Verdict recorded where the threshold is applied; the assert below reads it back.
            # The assert loop bails on its first failure, so computing these here is what makes
            # a later field's result knowable after an earlier one has failed.
            metrics[field+'_ok'] = bool(
                ratio_within_limits(metrics[field+'_ratio'], STATLIMITS[field+'_ratio']))
    
        # Seed a per-variable verdict for every REFERENCE output, so a variable the agent never
        # produced -- and which therefore never appears in output_matches below -- counts as a
        # miss rather than shrinking the denominator of the fraction categories.
        reference_output_names = list(reference_data_stats['data_summary'].get('output_range') or [])
        for ref_name in reference_output_names:
            metrics[f'output_nclasses_ok_{ref_name}'] = False
            metrics[f'output_fraction_ok_{ref_name}'] = False
    
        # check that input ranges match via 1-1 matching
        input_matches, input_match_costs = match_variables_by_hungarian(
            submitted_data_stats['input_range'],
            reference_data_stats['data_summary']['input_range'],
            weight_semantic=.95,
            weight_range=.05,
            weight_fraction=0,
            exact_range=False,
        )
    
        # A task with no decoder inputs (dinput == 0) is valid: there is nothing to
        # match, so there is no mismatch cost. np.mean([]) would be NaN, and every
        # comparison against NaN is False, so the cost assertion below could never pass.
        # Named for what it is: the mean Hungarian MATCHING cost, which is dominated
        # by name similarity and is forced to 0 for exactly-matching names before any
        # range term is computed. It is not a mean of the input_range_error_<var>
        # fields -- that is mean_input_range_error, recorded below.
        mean_input_cost = float(np.mean(input_match_costs)) if len(input_match_costs) else 0.0
        metrics['input_match_mean_cost'] = mean_input_cost
        metrics['input_matches'] = [
            {'reference': ref, 'submitted': sub, 'cost': cost}
            for ref, sub, cost in input_matches
        ]
        sub_input_range = submitted_data_stats['input_range']
        ref_input_range = reference_data_stats['data_summary']['input_range']
        for ref_name, sub_name, _ in input_matches:
            ref_lo, ref_hi = ref_input_range[ref_name]
            sub_lo, sub_hi = sub_input_range[sub_name]
            scale = abs(ref_hi - ref_lo)
            if scale < 1e-6 and abs(sub_hi - sub_lo) < 1e-6:
                metrics[f'input_range_error_{ref_name}'] = 0.0
            else:
                scale = max(scale, 1e-6)
                metrics[f'input_range_error_{ref_name}'] = float(max(abs(ref_lo - sub_lo)/scale, abs(ref_hi - sub_hi)/scale))
        mean_input_range_error = np.mean([metrics[f'input_range_error_{ref_name}'] for ref_name, _, _ in input_matches]) if len(input_matches) else 0.0
        metrics['mean_input_range_error'] = mean_input_range_error
        # Recorded ONLY when there is something to match. A task with no decoder inputs
        # (allen2p: dinput == 0, input_range == {}) has no input ranges to compare, so leaving
        # the key unset scores the category undefined and drops it from the mean -- rather than
        # awarding a free 1.0 for a check that never happened. Matches undefined_categories()
        # in lesion_analysis.py, which singles out this same case. The assert below is guarded
        # by the same condition, so it never reads a key that was not written.
        if len(input_matches):
            metrics['input_range_ok'] = bool(
                mean_input_range_error <= STATLIMITS['input_range_error'])
    
        # match outputs based on range, fraction, and semantic similarity of names
        output_matches, output_match_costs = match_outputs(
            submitted_data_stats, reference_data_stats
        )
        metrics['output_matches'] = [
            {'reference': ref, 'submitted': sub, 'cost': cost}
            for ref, sub, cost in output_matches
        ]
    
        # As above: the mean matching cost, not a mean of output_fraction_error_<var>.
        mean_output_match_cost = float(np.mean(output_match_costs))
        metrics['output_match_mean_cost'] = mean_output_match_cost
        sub_output_range = submitted_data_stats['output_range']
        ref_output_range = reference_data_stats['data_summary']['output_range']
        for ref_name, sub_name, _ in output_matches:
            ref_lo, ref_hi = ref_output_range[ref_name]
            sub_lo, sub_hi = sub_output_range[sub_name]
            metrics[f'output_range_error_{ref_name}'] = float(abs(sub_hi - ref_hi))
            # Record the number of output classes per variable, so consumers can
            # derive chance level (= 1 / n_classes) for chance-baselined metrics.
            # For integer-coded categorical outputs, n_classes = hi + 1.
            # `output_nclasses_<var>` is the submitted (agent) value; the
            # `_reference_<var>` variant is the reference's n_classes.
            metrics[f'output_nclasses_{ref_name}'] = int(round(sub_hi) + 1)
            metrics[f'output_nclasses_reference_{ref_name}'] = int(round(ref_hi) + 1)
            # fraction error per output
            ref_fracs = sorted(reference_data_stats['data_summary']['output_fractions'][ref_name].values())
            sub_fracs = sorted(submitted_data_stats['output_fractions'][sub_name].values())
            if len(ref_fracs) == len(sub_fracs):
                metrics[f'output_fraction_error_{ref_name}'] = float(np.sum(np.abs(np.array(ref_fracs) - np.array(sub_fracs))))
            else:
                metrics[f'output_fraction_error_{ref_name}'] = None
    
            metrics[f'output_nclasses_ok_{ref_name}'] = bool(
                metrics[f'output_range_error_{ref_name}'] <= STATLIMITS['output_range_error'])
            # A None error means the class counts differ, so there is no comparable fraction
            # vector. That scores as a miss, but is NOT asserted on below -- the nclasses check
            # already fails that case, and asserting here too would change what the suite
            # rejects. Verdict and assert diverge only here, deliberately.
            frac_error = metrics[f'output_fraction_error_{ref_name}']
            metrics[f'output_fraction_ok_{ref_name}'] = bool(
                frac_error is not None and frac_error <= STATLIMITS['output_fraction_error'])

A decision that differs from the expert's is acceptable if it is equally well justified; decisions that are poorly justified will be flagged as concerning or incorrect.\n24\t\n25\t## Reference Information\n26\t\n27\t- The reference **papers**:\n28\t  - \"A brain-wide map of neural activity during complex behaviour\" describes how the data were collected and is in the file `/app/datapaper.pdf`.\n29\t  - \"Exploiting correlations across trials and behavioral sessions to improve neural decoding\" describes how the code were used and is in the file `/app/methodpaper.pdf`.\n30\t  - A white paper about the data architecture is in `/app/dataarchitecture.pdf`.\n31\t- Some parts of the papers that describe the experiment and processing have been copied to the file `/app/methods.txt`. \n32\t- **Code** from the methods paper are in the directory `/app/code`.\n33\t- **Data** from the data paper are in the directory `/app/data`. \n34\t- **Documentation** about how to access the data can be found at https://docs.internationalbrainlab.org/public_docs/public_introduction.html. Documentation for `ONE`, `ibllib` and `iblatlas` is also downloaded to `/app/ibl_docs/`.\n35\t\n36\t## Decoder Task\n37\t\n38\tTemporally align based on stimulus onset\n39\t\n40\t### Decoder Inputs:\n41\t- Time since stimulus onset, continuous, time-varying\n42\t- Trial number in block, continuous, per-trial\n43\t\n44\t### Decoder Outputs\n45\t- Choice, binary, per-trial, left = 0, right = 1\n46\t- Prior probability of left, per-trial, 0.2 -> 0, 0.5 -> 1, 0.8 -> 2\n47\t- Wheel speed discretized into 3 bins, time-varying\n48\t- Whisker motion energy discretized into 3 bins, time-varying\n49\t\n50\t## Target Data Format\n51\t\n52\t- Save the full converted dataset to the pickle file `/app/converted_data.pkl`.\n53\t- All datasets must be converted into the following Python dictionary structure:\n54\t\n55\t```python\n56\tdata = {\n57\t    'neural': [  # list of sessions\n58\t        [  # list of trials for session 1\n59\t            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\n60\t            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # trial 2\n61\t            ...\n62\t        ],\n63\t        [  # list of trials for session 2\n64\t            ...\n65\t        ],\n66\t        ...\n67\t    ],\n68\t\n69\t    'input': [  # list of sessions\n70\t        [  # list of trials for session 1\n71\t            input_data,  # stimulus/task variables, shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input)\n72\t            ...\n73\t        ],\n74\t        ...\n75\t    ],\n76\t\n77\t    'output': [  # list of sessions\n78\t        [  # list of trials for session 1\n79\t            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)\n80\t            ...\n81\t        ],\n82\t        ...\n83\t    ],\n84\t\n85\t    'subjects': list of str, # ids of all subjects, length n_subjects\n86\t    'subject_idx': shape (n_sessions,), # index into subjects for each session\n87\t\n88\t    'brain_regions': list of str, # names of the brain regions recorded from, e.g. ALM, V1\n89\t    'brain_region_idx': [ # list of sessions\n90\t        neuron_region_idx, # shape: (n_neurons,)\n91\t    ], # index into `brain_regions` for each neuron\n92\t\n93\t    'input_names': list of str, # names for each input, of length n_input\n94\t    'output_names': list of str, # names of each output, of length n_output\n95\t    'output_values': [ # list of length n_output\n96\t        [ output_val0, ... ], # list of str of length d_output[0], name of each output value\n97\t        ...\n98\t    ],\n99\t\n100\t    'metadata': {\n101\t        'task_description': str, # description of output tasks\n102\t        'time_bin_size': float, # length of time bin in ms\n103\t        'temporal_alignment_event': str, # description of alignment event\n104\t        'off_start': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to start of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n105\t        'off_end': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to end of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n106\t        ...\n107\t    }\n108\t}\n109\t```\n110\t\n111\t### Key Format Requirements\n112\t\n113\t- **neural**: Neural activity data (e.g., firing rates, spike counts) organized by session and trial\n114\t  - Dimensions: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) for each trial.\n115\t  - Time bins should be the same size for all trials and sessions. \n116\t  - There needs to be at least two trials within each session in order to evaluate the decoder performance.\n117\t\n118\t- **input**: Variables that serve as inputs **to the decoder**\n119\t  - These are **decoder inputs**. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n120\t  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n121\t    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n122\t    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n123\t    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n124\t  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n125\t  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n126\t  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n127\t\n128\t- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n129\t  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n130\t  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \n131\t  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\n132\t  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n133\t  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n134\t\n135\t- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n136\t- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n137\t  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n138\t\n139\t- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n140\t- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n141\t\n142\t- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n143\t  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n144\t\n145\t- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n146\t  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n147\t- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n148\t  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n149\t\n150\t- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n151\t  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n152\t  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n153\t  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \n154\t  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n155\t  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n156\t\n157\t## Python environment\n158\t\n159\t- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n160\t- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n161\t- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n162\t\n163\t## Decoder Reference\n164\t\n165\t- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n166\t- Optional arguments:\n167\t  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n168\t  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n169\t  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n170\t- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n171\t\n172\t### Purpose\n173\t\n174\tThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n175\t1. Data structure is correct - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n176\t2. Dimensions are consistent - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n177\t3. Values are sensible - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n178\t4. Decoder can successfully train and predict\n179\t5. Poor performance indicates data formatting issues that need investigation\n180\t\n181\t### Consistency requirements\n182\t\n183\tYour processing and formatting must **match the reference papers and code** with respect to:\n184\t- Loading of data\n185\t- Temporal alignment of different time series streams (neural, inputs, outputs)\n186\t- Processing of neural, input, and output data streams\n187\t- Curation of data: filtering of low-quality neurons, trials, sessions, and mice.\n188\t\n189\tTo check consistency, you must compare statistics available in the reference paper and your converted dataset. \n190\t\n191\tWhenever possible, invent **SANITY CHECKS** that your loading and processing matches the reference paper and code. \n192\t\n193\tDiscrepancies are only allowed if required by the Decoder Input and Decoder Output specifications above, or the task of training a neural decoder.\n194\t\n195\tCarefully verify your work after every step. When you find mistakes, document and fix them immediately. Be critical of results **after every step of processing**. \n196\t\n197\tYou will be assessed on whether the decisions you make on how to load, filter, process, align, reformat, and save the data are reasonable and match the reference paper and code and these instructions. During testing, the reference version of `/app/train_decoder.py` will be run on your converted data. Data statistics and decoder accuracy will be compared to those achieved by human-written conversion code. \n198\t\n199\t---\n200\t\n201\t## Conversion Workflow\n202\t\n203\t**IMPORTANT**: Follow these steps in order. list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # trial 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        [  # list of trials for session 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'input': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            input_data,  # stimulus/task variables, shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'output': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'subjects': list of str, # They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n\n## Python environment\n\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n\n## Decoder Reference\n\n- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n- Optional arguments:\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n\n### Purpose\n\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n1. What processing is involved in computing `output` *wheel_speed*?\n287\t\n288\ti. Three steps. The wheel is recorded only when it moves, so `SessionLoader` first interpolates the position onto an even 1000 Hz grid and differentiates it into a velocity, applying a 20 Hz Butterworth low pass while doing so; the speed is the absolute value of that velocity, in radians per second. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n377\t\n378\ti. The API handles most of it. Missing data is dropped: A trial whose window is not spanned by the wheel or the camera is dropped; A session left with no unit or fewer than two trials is dropped.\n379\t\n380\tii. Mostly are missing data that we drop from the final results.\n404\t\n405\t## 10-a. What are the most time-consuming steps of the code?\n406\t\n407\ti. Reading the spike sorting, the one expensive call:\n410\t```python\n411\tspikes, clusters, channels = loader.load_spike_sorting(check_hash=False)\n412\t```\n413\t\n414\tiii. The cost is mainly file I/O.\n415\t\n416\t## 10-b. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n417\t\n418\ti. Two loops run once per trial, one resampling the behavioural traces and one binning the spikes. ap.add_argument('--show-processing',action='store_true'); args=ap.parse_args()\n345\t    sample=args.sample\n346\t    base,update=make_ones(); eids,left,right=candidate_eids(base,update)\n347\t delta-F/F is therefore not applicable.\n56\t- Reference cache script uses `ONE(base_url='https://openalyx.internationalbrainlab.org', cache_dir=...)` and brainbox loaders rather than direct ALF file reads.\n57\t- Dataset selection comes from the frozen `bwm_release.csv` (brain-wide map) or reproducible-ephys EID list.\n58\t- Reference temporal processing is stimulus aligned: `stimOn_times`, window `[-0.5, +1.5]` s, 20 ms bins (100 bins/trial).\n59\t- Reference decoded behaviors are choice, reward, block (`probabilityLeft`), wheel speed, and whisker motion energy. The present task requires choice, prior-left, wheel-speed tertile, and whisker-motion-energy tertile; reward is not requested.\n60\t- Continuous wheel and whisker streams are loaded with ONE and interpolated within each trial interval. Whisker motion energy prefers left camera and falls back to right camera.\n61\t- The quality hook is `clusters_labeled['label'] >= qc`; `qc=1` would retain good units. However, `prepare_data` does not pass `qc`, so the reference cached neural arrays retain all clusters and only store `(label >= 1)` as `good_clusters` metadata. The conversion should follow this all-cluster behavior unless the papers impose a stronger curation rule.\n62\t- Trial masking can remove no-choice trials, invalid event timestamps, out-of-range reaction times, and trials longer than 10 s (the latter is explicitly passed by `prepare_data`). The unbiased 0.5 block is optionally removable, but must be retained here because it is a required prior class.\n63\t- Reference neural arrays are produced trial-by-time-by-neuron and must be transposed to neuron-by-time for the requested target structure.\n64\t- Reference cache randomly partitions trials 70/10/20 after alignment; the target pickle should preserve the full curated trials because the supplied decoder handles splitting.\n65\t- `align_spike_behavior` is intended to combine behavior availability and trial masks. Its use of Python `and` on mask lists is potentially fragile and will be checked rather than copied blindly.\n66\t\n67\t---\n68\t\n69\t## Step 2: Dataset Exploration\n70\t**Status**: COMPLETE\n71\t\n72\t### Data Structure\n73\t- Data are an IBL ONE cache rooted at `/app/data/one_cache`; all scientific objects were inspected through `one.api.ONE` and brainbox loaders, never by directly reading source files.\n74\t- ONE release tables present:\n75\t  - `2022_Q4_IBL_et_al_BWM`: 354 sessions, 115 subjects, 38,814 indexed datasets.\n76\t  - `2025_Q3_IBL_et_al_BWM`: 459 sessions, 139 subjects, 5,339 revised/additional datasets.\n77\t  - `Brainwidemap`: 480 indexed sessions, 143 subjects, 76,563 datasets; 459 sessions contain core ephys data.\n78\t- Native organization is lab/`Subjects`/subject/date/sequence, with ALF collections `alf`, `alf/probeXX/pykilosort`, and raw-ephys collections.\n79\t- Core trial data are a parquet aggregate (`_ibl_trials.table.pqt`) with 13 float64 columns: `goCue_times`, `response_times`, `choice`, `stimOn_times`, `contrastLeft`, `contrastRight`, `feedback_times`, `feedbackType`, `rewardVolume`, `probabilityLeft`, `firstMovement_times`, and interval start/end.\n80\t- Wheel is an ALF object with float64 `timestamps` and `position`; the sampled example had 890,708 points.\n81\t- Whisker motion energy is stored as float64 `leftCamera.ROIMotionEnergy` / `rightCamera.ROIMotionEnergy`, paired to camera `times`; the example had 299,749 left and 742,128 right samples.\n82\t- Per-probe spike sorting provides spike `times`, `clusters`, `depths`, `amps` and cluster/channel metadata including `label`, `acronym`, `atlas_id`, depths, UUIDs, and QC metrics. Mice turn a wheel to move a grating; trial priors are left probabilities 0.2, 0.5, or 0.8.\n133\t- Alignment for the supplied Zhang cache code is stimulus onset with 20 ms spike bins over [-0.5, +1.5] s (100 bins).\n134\t- Data-paper binary stimulus/choice/feedback decoding used L1 logistic regression, inverse-class-frequency weighting, and balanced accuracy.\n135\t- Data-paper wheel decoding averages wheel speed/velocity in non-overlapping 20 ms bins; spikes are similarly binned. Its original wheel-specific analysis is movement aligned (-0.2 to +1.0 s) with ten preceding bins of causal neural history. The present task instead explicitly requires stimulus alignment, so the Zhang stimulus window takes precedence.\n136\t- Whisker motion energy is mean absolute pixel difference between adjacent frames within a DLC-defined whisker-pad ROI, at the camera temporal resolution. It is already computed; the DLC likelihood ≥0.9 rule applies to landmark estimates used in analyses, not to postcomputed motion-energy samples.\n137\t- Multiple probes in a session are combined because they are not independent sessions.\n138\t- The data paper used nested fivefold cross-validation; ten repeats for binary variables and two for wheel variables. The companion analysis generally required ≥250 trials.\n139\t- The methods paper evaluates scalar choice/prior per trial and dynamic wheel speed/whisker motion energy per timepoint. Discrete variables use accuracy/AUC; continuous dynamic variables use Pearson correlation. Its example figure prints accuracies 0.71 and 0.90 for discrete examples, but these are illustrative session/model values rather than release-wide targets for the supplied categorical decoder.\n140\t\n141\t### Curation Steps\n142\t\n143\t**Neuron curation rules**:\n144\t- Data-release insertion QC: exclude recordings with major RIGOR artifacts, unrecovered probe tracts, or unresolved histology alignment.\n145\t- Analysis units are well-isolated clusters passing all three RIGOR single-unit criteria: amplitude >50 µV, noise cutoff <20 µV, and refractory-period-violation criterion. In ALF metrics this corresponds to `label >= 1` (75,708 units).\n146\t- Data-paper region analyses further restrict to Allen CCF gray matter, at least five well-isolated neurons per session/region, and at least two sessions per region.\n147\t- Although Zhang `prepare_data` caches all clusters and stores good-unit labels only as metadata, the data paper’s stated analysis curation uses well-isolated units. This discrepancy is explicitly resolved in Step 4.\n148\t\n149\t**Trial curation rules**:\n150\t- Exclude trials missing choice, `probabilityLeft`, feedback type, feedback time, stimulus onset, or first-movement time.\n151\t- Exclude trials with stimulus-onset-to-first-movement latency outside 0.08–2.00 s.\n152\t- Release sessions require ≥250 trials, ≥90% correct on 100% contrast trials for both left and right blocks, ≥3 incorrect trials, and hardware/task QC.\n153\t- Retain 0.5-prior trials because prior=0.5 is a required decoder class, even though reference code can optionally exclude the initial unbiased block.\n154\t\n155\t### Decoders Trained\n156\t| Decoded variable | Accuracy / metric |\n157\t|------------------|-------------------|\n158\t| Choice | Accuracy/AUC in methods paper; Raw 0/no-choice excluded. |\n201\t| Trial `probabilityLeft` | `output[1,:]` | 0.2→0, 0.5→1, 0.8→2; broadcast across bins | `bin_behaviors` (`block`) | Retain unbiased block. |\n202\t| Wheel `timestamps`, `position` | `output[2,:]` | Brainbox interpolation to uniform samples, low-pass filtered velocity, absolute value for speed, average within each 20 ms trial bin, then global tertiles→0/1/2 | `brainbox.behavior.wheel.interpolate_position`, `velocity_filtered`; Zhang wheel loader | Speed is magnitude, not signed velocity. |\n203\t| Left (fallback right) camera `times` and `ROIMotionEnergy` | `output[3,:]` | Match same-camera timestamps; average samples in each 20 ms bin; global tertiles→0/1/2 | Zhang `load_target_behavior`, `get_behavior_per_interval` | Prefer left exactly as reference code; fallback right only if unavailable. |\n204\t| Session subject | `subjects`, `subject_idx` | Unique sorted subject strings; session index mapping | ONE session table/API | Session order deterministic by EID. |\n205\t| Cluster `acronym` / atlas metadata | `brain_regions`, `brain_region_idx` | Preserve Beryl/Allen acronym returned by merged brainbox clusters; global sorted vocabulary | `SpikeSortingLoader.merge_clusters` | Unknown/missing labels excluded with non-gray/invalid units or mapped to `void` only if unavoidable. |\n206\t\n207\t### Key Decisions\n208\t1. **Cohort**: Begin with all 459 BWM ephys sessions and retain sessions with loadable full trials, wheel, and paired motion-energy/timestamp data. Preliminary maximum is 445 sessions. This preserves the complete source release subject to task-required streams.\n209\t2. **Neuron curation**: Retain well-isolated `label >= 1` units, following the data-paper analysis criteria (75,708 release-wide). Merge probes per session before binning.\n210\t3. **Gray matter**: Exclude units with invalid/void/root atlas labels; preserve all valid gray-matter acronyms. Do not apply the paper’s region-level ≥2-session inferential rule because this decoder is not testing each region independently.\n211\t4. **Trial curation**: Require finite choice, prior, feedback type/time, stimulus onset, and first movement; require raw choice ±1, prior exactly one of 0.2/0.5/0.8, reaction time 0.08–2.00 s, and complete 2 s coverage for both time-varying behaviors. Keep all valid contrasts and outcomes.\n212\t5. **Common time base**: 100 half-open 20 ms bins `[-0.5,1.5)` around stimulus onset; bin centers are the time input. Same edges are used for spikes, wheel, and whisker streams, preventing temporal drift.\n213\t6. **Behavior aggregation**: Average native samples falling in each bin. Linear interpolation is used only to bridge the high-rate wheel position onto a uniform grid before reference filtering; no extrapolation beyond available stream support. Missing/empty behavior bins invalidate that trial rather than being imputed.\n214\t7. **Discretization**: Compute 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles over all finite time-bin values from retained trials/sessions after processing. Apply fixed global thresholds to every session for comparable class meanings. Store physical-unit thresholds and class definitions in metadata. If tied quantiles occur, investigate rather than force arbitrary classes.\n215\t8. **Scalar representation**: Broadcast choice, prior, and trial number across all 100 bins. The supplied decoder flattens trial timepoints; broadcasting makes per-trial targets dimensionally consistent with dynamic outputs and avoids missing targets.\n216\t9. **Dtypes/storage**: Neural spike counts are stored as float32 because the supplied validator/trainer expects float32 (integer counts remain exact); input float32; output uint8; brain-region indices int32. Pickle protocol 5.\n217\t10. **Session exclusion**: Exclude sessions with <2 valid trials or zero curated neurons. Log every reason and count. No trial/session is dropped silently.\n218\t11. **Revision handling**: Resolve exact relative paths/revisions through ONE cache records. Where aggregate metadata omits the revision component, repair only ONE’s in-memory record before invoking `ONE.load_dataset`; never directly read scientific files.\n219\t12. **Output metadata**: `time_bin_size=20.0` ms, alignment=`visual stimulus onset (stimOn_times)`, `off_start=-0.5`, `off_end=1.5`, plus EIDs, subjects, trial indices, cameras used, quantile thresholds, filtering counts, and source release.\n220\t\n221\t### Planned Sanity Checks\n222\t- [ ] ONE-loaded trial 5 choice/prior equals converted classes via `np.allclose` after inverse mapping.\n223\t- [ ] Recompute one trial’s spike histogram directly from ONE/brainbox-loaded spike arrays and compare the full neuron×time matrix with `np.allclose`.\n224\t- [ ] Recompute wheel and whisker binned values/classes for three trials from separately ONE-loaded streams and compare with `np.allclose`.\n225\t- [ ] Verify all trial arrays have exactly 100 bins and all session lists have matching trial counts.\n226\t- [ ] Verify bin centers are identical across all trials and span -0.49 to +1.49 s.\n227\t- [ ] Verify choice/prior/trial-number rows are constant within each trial; Mice turn a wheel to move a grating; trial priors are left probabilities 0.2, 0.5, or 0.8.\n- Alignment for the supplied Zhang cache code is stimulus onset with 20 ms spike bins over [-0.5, +1.5] s (100 bins).\n- Data-paper binary stimulus/choice/feedback decoding used L1 logistic regression, inverse-class-frequency weighting, and balanced accuracy.\n- Data-paper wheel decoding averages wheel speed/velocity in non-overlapping 20 ms bins; spikes are similarly binned. Its original wheel-specific analysis is movement aligned (-0.2 to +1.0 s) with ten preceding bins of causal neural history. The present task instead explicitly requires stimulus alignment, so the Zhang stimulus window takes precedence.\n- Whisker motion energy is mean absolute pixel difference between adjacent frames within a DLC-defined whisker-pad ROI, at the camera temporal resolution. It is already computed; the DLC likelihood ≥0.9 rule applies to landmark estimates used in analyses, not to postcomputed motion-energy samples.\n- Multiple probes in a session are combined because they are not independent sessions.\n- The data paper used nested fivefold cross-validation; ten repeats for binary variables and two for wheel variables. The companion analysis generally required ≥250 trials.\n- The methods paper evaluates scalar choice/prior per trial and dynamic wheel speed/whisker motion energy per timepoint. Discrete variables use accuracy/AUC; continuous dynamic variables use Pearson correlation. Its example figure prints accuracies 0.71 and 0.90 for discrete examples, but these are illustrative session/model values rather than release-wide targets for the supplied categorical decoder.\n\n### Curation Steps\n\n**Neuron curation rules**:\n- Data-release insertion QC: exclude recordings with major RIGOR artifacts, unrecovered probe tracts, or unresolved histology alignment.\n- Analysis units are well-isolated clusters passing all three RIGOR single-unit criteria: amplitude >50 µV, noise cutoff <20 µV, and refractory-period-violation criterion. In ALF metrics this corresponds to `label >= 1` (75,708 units).\n- Data-paper region analyses further restrict to Allen CCF gray matter, at least five well-isolated neurons per session/region, and at least two sessions per region.\n- Although Zhang `prepare_data` caches all clusters and stores good-unit labels only as metadata, the data paper’s stated analysis curation uses well-isolated units. This discrepancy is explicitly resolved in Step 4.\n\n**Trial curation rules**:\n- Exclude trials missing choice, `probabilityLeft`, feedback type, feedback time, stimulus onset, or first-movement time.\n- Exclude trials with stimulus-onset-to-first-movement latency outside 0.08–2.00 s.\n- Release sessions require ≥250 trials, ≥90% correct on 100% contrast trials for both left and right blocks, ≥3 incorrect trials, and hardware/task QC.\n- Retain 0.5-prior trials because prior=0.5 is a required decoder class, even though reference code can optionally exclude the initial unbiased block.\n\n### Decoders Trained\n| Decoded variable | Accuracy / metric |\n|------------------|-------------------|\n| Choice | Accuracy/AUC in methods paper; balanced accuracy in data paper; illustrative discrete example accuracy 0.71 |\n| Prior | Accuracy/AUC in methods paper; illustrative discrete example accuracy 0.90 |\n| Wheel speed | Pearson correlation (methods paper) or R² (data paper continuous decoder); categorical tertiles required here |\n| Whisker motion energy | Pearson correlation in methods paper; categorical tertiles required here |\n\n---\n\n## Step 4: Check for Consistency\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Discrepancies Found\n| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Papers say | Resolution |\n|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|\n| Cohort | Example shell caches first 10 reproducible-ephys EIDs; A session is usable only if it has the required trial, wheel, spike, cluster, and paired motion-energy/timestamp streams; preliminary eligible count is 445.\n- Combine all probe insertions within a session and retain well-isolated (`label >= 1`) gray-matter units. Preserve Allen/Beryl region labels per neuron; do not impose the paper’s cross-session “two sessions per region” significance-analysis rule because the target decoder consumes whole-session populations rather than per-region hypothesis tests.\n- Apply data-paper trial validity and 0.08–2.00 s reaction-time rules. Keep 0.5-prior trials.\n- Use 100 non-overlapping 20 ms bins from -0.5 to +1.5 s around stimulus onset for neural counts, time input, wheel speed, and whisker motion energy.\n- Choice mapping follows the task, not raw IBL sign semantics: raw `choice=-1` (left) → 0 and `choice=+1` (right) → 1. Prior 0.2→0, 0.5→1, 0.8→2.\n- Any session with fewer than two valid trials or zero curated neurons will be excluded and reported.\n\n---\n\n## Step 5: Mapping Planning\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Variable Mapping\n| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |\n|-----------------|--------------|-----------|----------------------------|-------|\n| `spikes.times`, `spikes.clusters` + cluster `label` | `neural` | Merge probes; retain `label >= 1`; histogram counts in 100 bins from -0.5 to +1.5 s around stimulus onset; shape `(n_neurons,100)`, integer counts | `SpikeSortingLoader`, `merge_clusters`, `bin_spiking_data` | Preserve counts (not rates or z-scores) so no information is lost. |\n| Bin centers relative to `stimOn_times` | `input[0,:]` | Constant float32 vector `[-0.49, ..., 1.49]` s for every trial | Zhang `create_intervals` | Continuous time since stimulus onset. |\n| Trial order within contiguous `probabilityLeft` block | `input[1,:]` | Zero-based counter reset to 0 whenever prior changes; broadcast across 100 bins | Derived from trial table | Continuous per-trial context; computed before trial filtering so skipped trials do not renumber the experimental block. |\n| Trial `choice` | `output[0,:]` | Raw -1 (left)→0, +1 (right)→1; broadcast across bins | `bin_behaviors` | Task-specified semantics. Raw 0/no-choice excluded. |\n| Trial `probabilityLeft` | `output[1,:]` | 0.2→0, 0.5→1, 0.8→2; broadcast across bins | `bin_behaviors` (`block`) | Retain unbiased block. |\n| Wheel `timestamps`, `position` | `output[2,:]` | Brainbox interpolation to uniform samples, low-pass filtered velocity, absolute value for speed, average within each 20 ms trial bin, then global tertiles→0/1/2 | `brainbox.behavior.wheel.interpolate_position`, `velocity_filtered`; Zhang wheel loader | Speed is magnitude, not signed velocity. |\n| Left (fallback right) camera `times` and `ROIMotionEnergy` | `output[3,:]` | Match same-camera timestamps; average samples in each 20 ms bin; global tertiles→0/1/2 | Zhang `load_target_behavior`, `get_behavior_per_interval` | Prefer left exactly as reference code; fallback right only if unavailable. |\n| Session subject | `subjects`, `subject_idx` | Unique sorted subject strings; session index mapping | ONE session table/API | Session order deterministic by EID. |\n| Cluster `acronym` / atlas metadata | `brain_regions`, `brain_region_idx` | Preserve Beryl/Allen acronym returned by merged brainbox clusters; global sorted vocabulary | `SpikeSortingLoader.merge_clusters` | Unknown/missing labels excluded with non-gray/invalid units or mapped to `void` only if unavoidable. |\n\n### Key Decisions\n1. **Cohort**: Begin with all 459 BWM ephys sessions and retain sessions with loadable full trials, wheel, and paired motion-energy/timestamp data. Preliminary maximum is 445 sessions. This preserves the complete source release subject to task-required streams.\n2. **Neuron curation**: Retain well-isolated `label >= 1` units, following the data-paper analysis criteria (75,708 release-wide). Merge probes per session before binning.\n3. **Gray matter**: Exclude units with invalid/void/root atlas labels; preserve all valid gray-matter acronyms. Do not apply the paper’s region-level ≥2-session inferential rule because this decoder is not testing each region independently.\n4. **Trial curation**: Require finite choice, prior, feedback type/time, stimulus onset, and first movement; require raw choice ±1, prior exactly one of 0.2/0.5/0.8, reaction time 0.08–2.00 s, and complete 2 s coverage for both time-varying behaviors. Keep all valid contrasts and outcomes.\n5. **Common time base**: 100 half-open 20 ms bins `[-0.5,1.5)` around stimulus onset; bin centers are the time input. Same edges are used for spikes, wheel, and whisker streams, preventing temporal drift.\n6. **Behavior aggregation**: Average native samples falling in each bin. Linear interpolation is used only to bridge the high-rate wheel position onto a uniform grid before reference filtering; no extrapolation beyond available stream support. Missing/empty behavior bins invalidate that trial rather than being imputed.\n7. **Discretization**: Compute 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles over all finite time-bin values from retained trials/sessions after processing. Apply fixed global thresholds to every session for comparable class meanings. Store physical-unit thresholds and class definitions in metadata. If tied quantiles occur, investigate rather than force arbitrary classes.\n8. **Scalar representation**: Broadcast choice, prior, and trial number across all 100 bins. The supplied decoder flattens trial timepoints; broadcasting makes per-trial targets dimensionally consistent with dynamic outputs and avoids missing targets.\n9. **Dtypes/storage**: Neural spike counts are stored as float32 because the supplied validator/trainer expects float32 (integer counts remain exact); input float32; output uint8; brain-region indices int32. Pickle protocol 5.\n10. **Session exclusion**: Exclude sessions with <2 valid trials or zero curated neurons. Log every reason and count. No trial/session is dropped silently.\n11. **Revision handling**: Resolve exact relative paths/revisions through ONE cache records. Where aggregate metadata omits the revision component, repair only ONE’s in-memory record before invoking `ONE.load_dataset`; never directly read scientific files.\n12. **Output metadata**: `time_bin_size=20.0` ms, alignment=`visual stimulus onset (stimOn_times)`, `off_start=-0.5`, `off_end=1.5`, plus EIDs, subjects, trial indices, cameras used, quantile thresholds, filtering counts, and source release.\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [ ] ONE-loaded trial 5 choice/prior equals converted classes via `np.allclose` after inverse mapping.\n- [ ] Recompute one trial’s spike histogram directly from ONE/brainbox-loaded spike arrays and compare the full neuron×time matrix with `np.allclose`.\n- [ ] Recompute wheel and whisker binned values/classes for three trials from separately ONE-loaded streams and compare with `np.allclose`.\n- [ ] Verify all trial arrays have exactly 100 bins and all session lists have matching trial counts.\n- [ ] Verify bin centers are identical across all trials and span -0.49 to +1.49 s.\n- [ ] Verify choice/prior/trial-number rows are constant within each trial; dynamic outputs show temporal variation.\n- [ ] Verify output values are integer and exactly within declared categories; report global/session class fractions.\n- [ ] Compare total release/session/subject/unit/trial counts to paper and Steps 2–4, explaining only required-stream/filter reductions.\n- [ ] Verify per-session neuron region index length equals neural row count and global indices resolve valid labels.\n- [ ] Check off-by-one behavior at first/last bins using half-open edges and spike events exactly on boundaries.\n- [ ] Plot raw aligned streams, binned continuous streams, tertile classes, and neural raster for up to two sessions.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nImplemented `/app/convert_data.py` with required `--full`, `--sample`, and `--show-processing` modes. How are trials filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Four stages. (1) `trial_mask` requires finite values for `choice`, `probabilityLeft`, `feedbackType`, `feedback_times`, `stimOn_times`, `firstMovement_times`; `choice ∈ {-1,+1}` (drops no-response trials); `probabilityLeft ∈ {0.2,0.5,0.8}`; and reaction time (`firstMovement_times − stimOn_times`) in [0.08, 2.00] s. (2) A behavioural-coverage filter: wheel and camera traces are interpolated with `left=nan, right=nan`, and any trial with a non-finite sample in its 2 s window is dropped. (3) Trials in which *no curated neuron* fired a single spike over the whole window are dropped (39 trials dataset-wide). (4) Sessions retaining fewer than two trials, or zero curated neurons, raise and are skipped. 190,239 trials survive out of ~293,662 raw.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef trial_mask(trials):\n    required = ['choice', 'probabilityLeft', 'feedbackType', 'feedback_times',\n                'stimOn_times', 'firstMovement_times']\n    ...\n    m = np.ones(len(trials), dtype=bool)\n    for c in required:\n        m &= np.isfinite(trials[c].to_numpy(dtype=float))\n    ...\n    m &= np.isin(choice, [-1., 1.])\n    m &= np.isin(prior, [.2, .5, .8])\n    m &= (rt >= .08) & (rt <= 2.0)\n    return m\n```\n```python\n    complete = np.isfinite(wheel).all(1) & np.isfinite(whisk).all(1)\n    ...\n    if len(align) < 2:\n        raise RuntimeError(f'fewer than two complete valid trials ({len(align)})')\n    neural, regions, uuids, nspikes = load_binned_neural(base, eid, align)\n    # Trials with no spikes from any curated unit contain no neural observation\n    # and are rejected by the supplied validator. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Wheel speed* derived from?\n\ni. The ALF `wheel` object loaded through ONE — `_ibl_wheel.timestamps` and `_ibl_wheel.position` — from which a filtered velocity is computed with the brainbox wheel helpers; speed is its absolute value (rad/s).\n\nii.\n```python\ndef load_wheel_speed(base, eid, align):\n    w = base.load_object(eid, 'wheel', collection='alf')\n    ts = np.asarray(w['timestamps'], float)\n    pos = np.asarray(w['position'], float)\n    # Reference brainbox processing: 1 kHz interpolation then filtered derivative.\n    ipos, its = wheellib.interpolate_position(ts, pos, freq=1000)\n    vel, _ = wheellib.velocity_filtered(ipos, fs=1000)\n    return interp_trials(its, np.abs(vel), align), (ts, pos, its, vel)\n```\n\niii. Step 5 mapping table: \"Brainbox interpolation to uniform samples, low-pass filtered velocity, absolute value for speed … Speed is magnitude, not signed velocity\", citing `brainbox.behavior.wheel.interpolate_position` / `velocity_filtered` and the Zhang wheel loader.\n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Wheel speed*?\n\ni. Three steps. (1) The irregularly sampled wheel position is linearly interpolated onto a uniform 1 kHz grid (`interpolate_position(freq=1000)`), then differentiated with a 20 Hz, 8th-order Butterworth low-pass (`velocity_filtered(fs=1000)`, brainbox defaults — identical to what `SessionLoader.load_wheel` does internally); the absolute value gives speed. (2) The speed trace is **point-sampled by linear interpolation at the 100 bin centres** of each trial, with `left=nan, right=nan` so that trials not fully covered by the wheel stream are flagged and dropped; non-finite and duplicate timestamps are removed first. (3) The trace is then discretized (see 7-c).\n\nii.\n```python\ndef interp_trials(times, values, align):\n    \"\"\"Linear interpolation at common bin centers; no extrapolation.\"\"\"\n    ...\n    ok = np.isfinite(times) & np.isfinite(values)\n    times, values = times[ok], values[ok]\n    ...\n    keep = np.r_[True, np.diff(times) > 0]\n    times, values = times[keep], values[keep]\n    query = align[:, None] + BIN_CENTERS[None, :]\n    out = np.interp(query.ravel(), times, values, left=np.nan, right=np.nan)\n    return out.reshape(len(align), N_BINS).astype(np.float32)\n```\n\niii. Step 5 decision 6: \"Linear interpolation is used only to bridge the high-rate wheel position onto a uniform grid before reference filtering; no extrapolation beyond available stream support. Missing/empty behavior bins invalidate that trial rather than being imputed.\" (Note: the Step 5 mapping table text still says \"average within each 20 ms trial bin\", which the implemented code and the final metadata string — \"absolute speed sampled at bin centers\" — supersede.)\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Wheel speed* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Into three classes by **global** tertiles: after every session is processed, all retained wheel-speed bin values from all 445 sessions are pooled, the 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles are taken once, and the same two thresholds ([0.01477, 0.39721] rad/s) are applied to every session with `np.digitize`. The thresholds are stored in metadata; a guard rejects degenerate (non-increasing) tertiles.\n\nii.\n```python\n    wheel_vals = np.concatenate([s['wheel'].ravel() for s in sessions])\n    ...\n    thresholds = {'wheel': np.quantile(wheel_vals, [1/3, 2/3]).astype(float),\n                  'whisker': np.quantile(whisk_vals, [1/3, 2/3]).astype(float)}\n    for k,v in thresholds.items():\n        if not np.isfinite(v).all() or v[0] >= v[1]:\n            raise RuntimeError(f'invalid {k} tertiles {v}')\n    ...\n        wc=np.digitize(s['wheel'],thresholds['wheel']).astype(np.uint8)\n```\n\niii. Step 5 decision 7: \"Compute 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles over all finite time-bin values from retained trials/sessions after processing. Apply fixed global thresholds to every session for comparable class meanings. Store physical-unit thresholds and class definitions in metadata.\"\n\n## 7-d. How is `output` *Wheel speed* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. It is evaluated at exactly the same 100 bin centres, measured from the same `stimOn_times` vector used to bin the spikes, so the two share a time axis bin for bin. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Wheel speed*?\n\ni. Three steps. (1) The irregularly sampled wheel position is linearly interpolated onto a uniform 1 kHz grid (`interpolate_position(freq=1000)`), then differentiated with a 20 Hz, 8th-order Butterworth low-pass (`velocity_filtered(fs=1000)`, brainbox defaults — identical to what `SessionLoader.load_wheel` does internally); the absolute value gives speed. (2) The speed trace is **point-sampled by linear interpolation at the 100 bin centres** of each trial, with `left=nan, right=nan` so that trials not fully covered by the wheel stream are flagged and dropped; non-finite and duplicate timestamps are removed first. (3) The trace is then discretized (see 7-c).\n\nii.\n```python\ndef interp_trials(times, values, align):\n    \"\"\"Linear interpolation at common bin centers; no extrapolation.\"\"\"\n    ...\n    ok = np.isfinite(times) & np.isfinite(values)\n    times, values = times[ok], values[ok]\n    ...\n    keep = np.r_[True, np.diff(times) > 0]\n    times, values = times[keep], values[keep]\n    query = align[:, None] + BIN_CENTERS[None, :]\n    out = np.interp(query.ravel(), times, values, left=np.nan, right=np.nan)\n    return out.reshape(len(align), N_BINS).astype(np.float32)\n```\n\niii. Step 5 decision 6: \"Linear interpolation is used only to bridge the high-rate wheel position onto a uniform grid before reference filtering; no extrapolation beyond available stream support. Missing/empty behavior bins invalidate that trial rather than being imputed.\" (Note: the Step 5 mapping table text still says \"average within each 20 ms trial bin\", which the implemented code and the final metadata string — \"absolute speed sampled at bin centers\" — supersede.)\n\n## 7-c. Three steps. Sessions are held one at a time in each worker rather than all at once.\n\"\"\"Convert the IBL brain-wide map into the decoder format.\n\nUsage: python -u convert_data.py <outpicklefile> [--full | --sample] [--datadir DIR]\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport datetime\nimport os\nimport pickle\nimport time\nimport warnings\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nfrom tqdm import tqdm\n\n_zhang2025_seed = 'x5cidj2hy87s'\nnp.random.seed(sum(ord(c) for c in _zhang2025_seed) % 2**31)\n\n# the loader always pulls these four spike arrays\nimport brainbox.io.one as bio\nbio.SPIKES_ATTRIBUTES = ['clusters', 'times']\n\nfrom one.api import ONE, One\nfrom one.alf.exceptions import ALFWarning\nfrom brainbox.io.one import SessionLoader, SpikeSortingLoader\nfrom iblatlas.regions import BrainRegions\n\n# the trials table and the spike sorting are each listed at two revisions, and ONE warns\n# once per load that it is taking the later one, which is the one we want\nwarnings.filterwarnings('ignore', category=ALFWarning)\n\n# --- constants ---\n\nHERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\n# Directory holding the one_cache/ folder. The\n    client also resolves each dataset's current revision, which is what is on disk -- the\n    release tables list the pre-revision paths, so resolving from them alone finds no\n    trials. The metadata that resolution needs is cached under one_cache/.rest, so a run\n    does not have to reach Alyx.\n\n    datadir: directory holding the one_cache/ folder.\n    Sets the globals `one` and `subset_csv`; returns nothing.\n    \"\"\"\n    global one\n    global subset_csv\n    cache = os.path.join(datadir, ONE_CACHE_DIRNAME)\n    tables = os.path.join(cache, RELEASE)\n    client = dict(base_url=BASE_URL, silent=True, cache_dir=cache, tables_dir=tables,\n                  mode='remote')\n    try:\n        # No password: passing one forces re-authentication over the network, while the\n        # token the fetch cached needs no connection.\n        one = ONE(**client)\n    except Exception:\n        one = ONE(password=PASSWORD, **client)\n    one.alyx.default_expiry = REST_EXPIRY\n    # One.load_cache reads the parquet tables where they are; the OneAlyx override would\n    # ask Alyx for a newer copy first. In 'remote' mode nothing is loaded until this is\n    # called, and search() then returns no sessions at all, without raising.\n    One.load_cache(one, tables_dir=tables)\n    # Only the datalimit dataset ships this file; on the full dataset there is nothing to\n    # restrict to, and subset_csv stays None.\n    path = os.path.join(datadir, 'DATALIMIT_SUBSET.csv')\n    subset_csv = path if os.path.isfile(path) else None\n\n\n# --- sessions ---\n\ndef select_sessions():\n    \"\"\"Released sessions that have everything the decoder needs, grouped by subject.\"\"\"\n\n    required = ['spikes.times.npy', 'spikes.clusters.npy',          # ephys\n                '_ibl_trials.table.pqt',                            # task\n                '_ibl_wheel.position.npy', '_ibl_wheel.timestamps.npy']\n\n    keep = set(one.search(query_type='local', datasets=required))\n    keep &= (set(one.search(query_type='local', datasets=['leftCamera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy',\n                                                          '_ibl_leftCamera.times.npy']))\n             | set(one.search(query_type='local', datasets=['rightCamera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy',\n                                                            '_ibl_rightCamera.times.npy'])))\n    # The datalimit dataset ships a subset of the release (see DATALIMIT_SUBSET.csv). The ONE\n    # release index is unmodified and still lists every released session, so\n    # restrict to the eids named there -- otherwise a session that is not on disk\n    # would be fetched over the network. The full dataset has no such file, and every\n    # session the index lists is on disk.\n    # Compare in string space: one.search returns UUID objects while the csv column\n    # is str, so a plain set intersection is empty whatever the contents. keep must\n    # stay UUID-valued for the `eid in keep` test below.\n    if subset_csv is not None:\n        subset_eids = set(pd.read_csv(subset_csv).eid.astype(str))\n        keep = {eid for eid in keep if str(eid) in subset_eids}\n        if not keep:\n            raise SystemExit(f'No sessions matched {subset_csv}; refusing to continue.')\n\n    eids, info = one.search(query_type='local', details=True)\n    selected = {}\n    for eid, session in zip(eids, info):\n        if eid in keep:\n            selected.setdefault(session['subject'], []).append(str(eid))\n    return {subject: selected[subject] for subject in sorted(selected)}\n\n\ndef camera_view(eid):\n    \"\"\"The side camera this session has whisker motion energy for, left preferred.\"\"\"\n    for view in ('left', 'right'):\n        if len(one.list_datasets(eid, filename=f'{view}Camera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy',\n                                 query_type='local')):\n            return view\n    raise ValueError(f'no whisker motion energy for {eid}')\n\n\n# --- trials ---\n\ndef trial_variables(trials):\n    \"\"\"Choice, block prior and trial number in block, one row per trial.\"\"\"\n    # probabilityLeft is constant within a block, so a change of value starts a new block\n    block = (trials.probabilityLeft != trials.probabilityLeft.shift()).cumsum()\n\n    return pd.DataFrame({'choice': trials.choice.map(CHOICE),\n                         'prior': trials.probabilityLeft.map(PRIOR),\n                         'trial_in_block': trials.groupby(block).cumcount()})\n\n\ndef covered(times, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Trials whose window is spanned by this stream, allowing the one bin gap the reference allows.\"\"\"\n    start, stop = stim_on + T_START, stim_on + T_STOP\n    begin = np.searchsorted(times, start, side='right')      # first sample inside the window\n    end = np.searchsorted(times, stop, side='left') - 1       # last sample inside the window\n\n    # a trial with no sample at all, or a gap at either edge, has no usable trace\n    inside = begin <= end\n    first = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(begin, 0, times.size - 1)], np.inf)\n    last = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(end, 0, times.size - 1)], -np.inf)\n    return inside & (np.abs(start - first) <= BIN) & (np.abs(stop - last) <= BIN)\n\n\ndef usable_trials(trials, wheel_times, camera_times):\n    \"\"\"Trials the paper would keep, that also have a full wheel and camera window.\"\"\"\n    stim_on = trials.stimOn_times.to_numpy()\n    reaction = trials.firstMovement_times.to_numpy() - stim_on\n\n    keep = (reaction >= MIN_RT) & (reaction <= MAX_RT)          # NaN compares false, so those go too\n    keep &= trials.choice.isin(CHOICE).to_numpy()               # drops the no response trials\n    keep &= trials.probabilityLeft.isin(PRIOR).to_numpy()\n\n    return keep & covered(wheel_times, stim_on) & covered(camera_times, stim_on)\n\n\n# --- behavior ---\n\ndef window_slice(times, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Index range of each trial window, so a stream is sliced rather than rescanned per trial.\"\"\"\n    window_start = stim_on + T_START\n    window_stop = stim_on + T_STOP\n\n    # the samples are in time order, so each window is one contiguous range of them\n    begin = np.searchsorted(times, window_start)\n    end = np.searchsorted(times, window_stop)\n\n    return begin, end\n\n\ndef trial_traces(times, values, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"A continuous trace resampled onto the same time grid for every trial.\"\"\"\n    begin, end = window_slice(times, stim_on)\n\n    traces = []\n    for trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n        # one sample either side of the window, so the first and last bin centre are\n        # interpolated rather than clamped to the nearest sample inside it\n        first = max(begin[trial] - 1, 0)\n        last = end[trial] + 1\n\n        traces.append(np.interp(onset + TIME, times[first:last], values[first:last]))\n\n    return np.array(traces)\n\n\ndef discretize(trace):\n    \"\"\"Equal sized classes, split at percentiles of this session's own trace.\"\"\"\n    return np.digitize(trace, np.percentile(trace, SPLIT))\n\n\n# --- neural ---\n\ndef load_neural(eid):\n    \"\"\"Spike times and good clusters of a session, merged over its probes.\"\"\"\n    times, units, regions = [], [], []\n    for pid, name in zip(*one.eid2pid(eid)):\n        loader = SpikeSortingLoader(pid=pid, one=one, eid=eid, pname=name)\n\n        # spikes.clusters holds the row of the cluster table, so a per cluster flag\n        # can be indexed by it directly to say whether each spike survives\n        is_good = (clusters['label'] >= QC_LABEL) & in_brain\n        keep = is_good[spikes['clusters']]\n\n        # Beryl is the coarser atlas the reference code uses, e.g. DG-sg and DG-mo both become DG\n        regions.extend(brain_regions.acronym2acronym(clusters['acronym'][is_good], mapping='Beryl'))\n\n    times, units = np.concatenate(times), np.concatenate(units)\n\n    # one flat index per spike lets a single bincount fill the whole unit by bin grid\n        flat_index = spike_unit * N_BINS + bin_index\n        counts[trial] = np.bincount(flat_index, minlength=n_units * N_BINS).reshape(n_units, N_BINS)\n\n    return counts\n\n\n# --- session ---\n\ndef process_session(eid, subject):\n    \"\"\"One session as lists of per trial neural, input and output arrays.\"\"\"\n    loader = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)\n    loader.load_trials()\n    loader.load_wheel()\n    view = camera_view(eid)\n    loader.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\n\n    trials, wheel = loader.trials, loader.wheel\n    motion_energy = loader.motion_energy[f'{view}Camera']\n\n    variables = trial_variables(trials)                 # Neuropixels electrophysiology, not calcium imaging; delta-F/F is therefore not applicable.\n- Reference cache script uses `ONE(base_url='https://openalyx.internationalbrainlab.org', cache_dir=...)` and brainbox loaders rather than direct ALF file reads.\n- Dataset selection comes from the frozen `bwm_release.csv` (brain-wide map) or reproducible-ephys EID list.\n- Reference temporal processing is stimulus aligned: `stimOn_times`, window `[-0.5, +1.5]` s, 20 ms bins (100 bins/trial).\n- Reference decoded behaviors are choice, reward, block (`probabilityLeft`), wheel speed, and whisker motion energy. The present task requires choice, prior-left, wheel-speed tertile, and whisker-motion-energy tertile; reward is not requested.\n- Continuous wheel and whisker streams are loaded with ONE and interpolated within each trial interval.
