Mice turn a wheel to move a grating; trial priors are left probabilities 0.2, 0.5, or 0.8.\n- Alignment for the supplied Zhang cache code is stimulus onset with 20 ms spike bins over [-0.5, +1.5] s (100 bins).\n- Data-paper binary stimulus/choice/feedback decoding used L1 logistic regression, inverse-class-frequency weighting, and balanced accuracy.\n- Data-paper wheel decoding averages wheel speed/velocity in non-overlapping 20 ms bins; spikes are similarly binned. Its original wheel-specific analysis is movement aligned (-0.2 to +1.0 s) with ten preceding bins of causal neural history. The present task instead explicitly requires stimulus alignment, so the Zhang stimulus window takes precedence.\n- Whisker motion energy is mean absolute pixel difference between adjacent frames within a DLC-defined whisker-pad ROI, at the camera temporal resolution. It is already computed; the DLC likelihood ≥0.9 rule applies to landmark estimates used in analyses, not to postcomputed motion-energy samples.\n- Multiple probes in a session are combined because they are not independent sessions.\n- The data paper used nested fivefold cross-validation; ten repeats for binary variables and two for wheel variables. The companion analysis generally required ≥250 trials.\n- The methods paper evaluates scalar choice/prior per trial and dynamic wheel speed/whisker motion energy per timepoint. Discrete variables use accuracy/AUC; continuous dynamic variables use Pearson correlation. Its example figure prints accuracies 0.71 and 0.90 for discrete examples, but these are illustrative session/model values rather than release-wide targets for the supplied categorical decoder.\n\n### Curation Steps\n\n**Neuron curation rules**:\n- Data-release insertion QC: exclude recordings with major RIGOR artifacts, unrecovered probe tracts, or unresolved histology alignment.\n- Analysis units are well-isolated clusters passing all three RIGOR single-unit criteria: amplitude >50 µV, noise cutoff <20 µV, and refractory-period-violation criterion. In ALF metrics this corresponds to `label >= 1` (75,708 units).\n- Data-paper region analyses further restrict to Allen CCF gray matter, at least five well-isolated neurons per session/region, and at least two sessions per region.\n- Although Zhang `prepare_data` caches all clusters and stores good-unit labels only as metadata, the data paper’s stated analysis curation uses well-isolated units. This discrepancy is explicitly resolved in Step 4.\n\n**Trial curation rules**:\n- Exclude trials missing choice, `probabilityLeft`, feedback type, feedback time, stimulus onset, or first-movement time.\n- Exclude trials with stimulus-onset-to-first-movement latency outside 0.08–2.00 s.\n- Release sessions require ≥250 trials, ≥90% correct on 100% contrast trials for both left and right blocks, ≥3 incorrect trials, and hardware/task QC.\n- Retain 0.5-prior trials because prior=0.5 is a required decoder class, even though reference code can optionally exclude the initial unbiased block.\n\n### Decoders Trained\n| Decoded variable | Accuracy / metric |\n|------------------|-------------------|\n| Choice | Accuracy/AUC in methods paper; balanced accuracy in data paper; illustrative discrete example accuracy 0.71 |\n| Prior | Accuracy/AUC in methods paper; illustrative discrete example accuracy 0.90 |\n| Wheel speed | Pearson correlation (methods paper) or R² (data paper continuous decoder); categorical tertiles required here |\n| Whisker motion energy | Pearson correlation in methods paper; categorical tertiles required here |\n\n---\n\n## Step 4: Check for Consistency\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Discrepancies Found\n| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Papers say | Resolution |\n|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|\n| Cohort | Example shell caches first 10 reproducible-ephys EIDs; BWM mode samples one session per randomly chosen subject | Supplied BWM cache has the complete 459-session/699-insertion release; only 6/10 reproducible-ephys example EIDs overlap | Data paper defines 459 sessions, 699 insertions, 139 mice | Use the complete data-paper BWM release, not the non-overlapping example list. |\n| Unit filtering | Zhang `prepare_data` loads all Kilosort clusters and stores good labels as metadata | 621,733 total clusters; 75,708 with `label >= 1` | Data paper analyses exclude units failing amplitude, noise-cutoff, or refractory criteria; methods paper says all Kilosort units | Use `label >= 1` well-isolated units: this follows the data-paper curation explicitly required by the task, reduces noisy regressors, and makes full conversion tractable. Document difference from methods-paper implementation. |\n| Temporal alignment | Zhang cache uses stimulus onset, [-0.5,+1.5] s, 20 ms for all cached targets | All required streams cover this interval in eligible sessions | Methods paper uses choice stimulus-aligned, prior pre-stimulus, and dynamic behaviors movement-aligned; task explicitly requires stimulus alignment | Task requirement overrides target-specific alignments. Use the Zhang common stimulus-aligned 2 s/20 ms representation. |\n| Trial filtering | Zhang defaults exclude NaN events, no-choice and trials >10 s; optional RT and unbiased-block filters | Required fields and RT can be evaluated from trial table | Data paper excludes missing choice/prior/feedback/stimulus/movement and RT outside 0.08–2.00 s | Apply the stricter data-paper trial mask, but retain prior=0.5 trials because they are a required output class. |\n| Session count | Broad table indexes 480 sessions | 459 have core ephys; 445 have wheel plus paired left/right motion energy and timestamps | Public analyzed release has 459 sessions | Start from 459 release sessions; exclude 14 lacking required whisker stream, leaving 445 candidate sessions. This exclusion is required by decoder outputs. |\n| Trial-table revisions | Most revised tables are 2025-03-03 | Three core sessions use older revisions; two are otherwise behavior-complete | Papers do not discuss storage revisions | Resolve each table through ONE with its indexed revision; do not silently lose the two eligible sessions. |\n| Motion-energy camera | Reference loader prefers left and falls back to right | 436 left, 433 right, 445 with at least one paired stream | Data paper computes both camera ROIs | Prefer left to match code; use right only when left is unavailable, with matched camera timestamps. |\n| Array orientation | Reference cache stores trial × time × neuron | Target requires neuron × time per trial | N/A | Transpose each trial to neuron × time. |\n| Continuous outputs | Papers decode continuous wheel/whisker with correlation/R² | Raw streams are continuous | Task mandates three categorical bins | Discretize globally fitted valid-sample tertiles into classes 0/1/2; retain thresholds in metadata. |\n\n### Final Consistent Understanding\n- Source cohort is the 459-session BWM public release. A session is usable only if it has the required trial, wheel, spike, cluster, and paired motion-energy/timestamp streams; preliminary eligible count is 445.\n- Combine all probe insertions within a session and retain well-isolated (`label >= 1`) gray-matter units. Preserve Allen/Beryl region labels per neuron; do not impose the paper’s cross-session “two sessions per region” significance-analysis rule because the target decoder consumes whole-session populations rather than per-region hypothesis tests.\n- Apply data-paper trial validity and 0.08–2.00 s reaction-time rules. Keep 0.5-prior trials.\n- Use 100 non-overlapping 20 ms bins from -0.5 to +1.5 s around stimulus onset for neural counts, time input, wheel speed, and whisker motion energy.\n- Choice mapping follows the task, not raw IBL sign semantics: raw `choice=-1` (left) → 0 and `choice=+1` (right) → 1. Prior 0.2→0, 0.5→1, 0.8→2.\n- Any session with fewer than two valid trials or zero curated neurons will be excluded and reported.\n\n---\n\n## Step 5: Mapping Planning\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Variable Mapping\n| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |\n|-----------------|--------------|-----------|----------------------------|-------|\n| `spikes.times`, `spikes.clusters` + cluster `label` | `neural` | Merge probes; retain `label >= 1`; histogram counts in 100 bins from -0.5 to +1.5 s around stimulus onset; shape `(n_neurons,100)`, integer counts | `SpikeSortingLoader`, `merge_clusters`, `bin_spiking_data` | Preserve counts (not rates or z-scores) so no information is lost. |\n| Bin centers relative to `stimOn_times` | `input[0,:]` | Constant float32 vector `[-0.49, ..., 1.49]` s for every trial | Zhang `create_intervals` | Continuous time since stimulus onset. |\n| Trial order within contiguous `probabilityLeft` block | `input[1,:]` | Zero-based counter reset to 0 whenever prior changes; broadcast across 100 bins | Derived from trial table | Continuous per-trial context; computed before trial filtering so skipped trials do not renumber the experimental block. |\n| Trial `choice` | `output[0,:]` | Raw -1 (left)→0, +1 (right)→1; broadcast across bins | `bin_behaviors` | Task-specified semantics. Raw 0/no-choice excluded. |\n| Trial `probabilityLeft` | `output[1,:]` | 0.2→0, 0.5→1, 0.8→2; broadcast across bins | `bin_behaviors` (`block`) | Retain unbiased block. |\n| Wheel `timestamps`, `position` | `output[2,:]` | Brainbox interpolation to uniform samples, low-pass filtered velocity, absolute value for speed, average within each 20 ms trial bin, then global tertiles→0/1/2 | `brainbox.behavior.wheel.interpolate_position`, `velocity_filtered`; Zhang wheel loader | Speed is magnitude, not signed velocity. |\n| Left (fallback right) camera `times` and `ROIMotionEnergy` | `output[3,:]` | Match same-camera timestamps; average samples in each 20 ms bin; global tertiles→0/1/2 | Zhang `load_target_behavior`, `get_behavior_per_interval` | Prefer left exactly as reference code; fallback right only if unavailable. |\n| Session subject | `subjects`, `subject_idx` | Unique sorted subject strings; session index mapping | ONE session table/API | Session order deterministic by EID. |\n| Cluster `acronym` / atlas metadata | `brain_regions`, `brain_region_idx` | Preserve Beryl/Allen acronym returned by merged brainbox clusters; global sorted vocabulary | `SpikeSortingLoader.merge_clusters` | Unknown/missing labels excluded with non-gray/invalid units or mapped to `void` only if unavoidable. |\n\n### Key Decisions\n1. **Cohort**: Begin with all 459 BWM ephys sessions and retain sessions with loadable full trials, wheel, and paired motion-energy/timestamp data. Preliminary maximum is 445 sessions. This preserves the complete source release subject to task-required streams.\n2. **Neuron curation**: Retain well-isolated `label >= 1` units, following the data-paper analysis criteria (75,708 release-wide). Merge probes per session before binning.\n3. **Gray matter**: Exclude units with invalid/void/root atlas labels; preserve all valid gray-matter acronyms. Do not apply the paper’s region-level ≥2-session inferential rule because this decoder is not testing each region independently.\n4. **Trial curation**: Require finite choice, prior, feedback type/time, stimulus onset, and first movement; require raw choice ±1, prior exactly one of 0.2/0.5/0.8, reaction time 0.08–2.00 s, and complete 2 s coverage for both time-varying behaviors. Keep all valid contrasts and outcomes.\n5. **Common time base**: 100 half-open 20 ms bins `[-0.5,1.5)` around stimulus onset; bin centers are the time input. Same edges are used for spikes, wheel, and whisker streams, preventing temporal drift.\n6. **Behavior aggregation**: Average native samples falling in each bin. Linear interpolation is used only to bridge the high-rate wheel position onto a uniform grid before reference filtering; no extrapolation beyond available stream support. Missing/empty behavior bins invalidate that trial rather than being imputed.\n7. **Discretization**: Compute 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles over all finite time-bin values from retained trials/sessions after processing. Apply fixed global thresholds to every session for comparable class meanings. Store physical-unit thresholds and class definitions in metadata. If tied quantiles occur, investigate rather than force arbitrary classes.\n8. **Scalar representation**: Broadcast choice, prior, and trial number across all 100 bins. The supplied decoder flattens trial timepoints; broadcasting makes per-trial targets dimensionally consistent with dynamic outputs and avoids missing targets.\n9. **Dtypes/storage**: Neural spike counts are stored as float32 because the supplied validator/trainer expects float32 (integer counts remain exact); input float32; output uint8; brain-region indices int32. Pickle protocol 5.\n10. **Session exclusion**: Exclude sessions with <2 valid trials or zero curated neurons. Log every reason and count. No trial/session is dropped silently.\n11. **Revision handling**: Resolve exact relative paths/revisions through ONE cache records. Where aggregate metadata omits the revision component, repair only ONE’s in-memory record before invoking `ONE.load_dataset`; never directly read scientific files.\n12. **Output metadata**: `time_bin_size=20.0` ms, alignment=`visual stimulus onset (stimOn_times)`, `off_start=-0.5`, `off_end=1.5`, plus EIDs, subjects, trial indices, cameras used, quantile thresholds, filtering counts, and source release.\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [ ] ONE-loaded trial 5 choice/prior equals converted classes via `np.allclose` after inverse mapping.\n- [ ] Recompute one trial’s spike histogram directly from ONE/brainbox-loaded spike arrays and compare the full neuron×time matrix with `np.allclose`.\n- [ ] Recompute wheel and whisker binned values/classes for three trials from separately ONE-loaded streams and compare with `np.allclose`.\n- [ ] Verify all trial arrays have exactly 100 bins and all session lists have matching trial counts.\n- [ ] Verify bin centers are identical across all trials and span -0.49 to +1.49 s.\n- [ ] Verify choice/prior/trial-number rows are constant within each trial; dynamic outputs show temporal variation.\n- [ ] Verify output values are integer and exactly within declared categories; report global/session class fractions.\n- [ ] Compare total release/session/subject/unit/trial counts to paper and Steps 2–4, explaining only required-stream/filter reductions.\n- [ ] Verify per-session neuron region index length equals neural row count and global indices resolve valid labels.\n- [ ] Check off-by-one behavior at first/last bins using half-open edges and spike events exactly on boundaries.\n- [ ] Plot raw aligned streams, binned continuous streams, tertile classes, and neural raster for up to two sessions.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nImplemented `/app/convert_data.py` with required `--full`, `--sample`, and `--show-processing` modes. Start from the 459-session BWM ephys release.\n2. Require trials, wheel, spikes/clusters, and paired camera motion energy/timestamps.\n3. Merge probes within each session.\n4. Keep well-isolated clusters (`label >= 1`), remap Allen acronyms to Beryl, and exclude `root`/`void`.\n5. Exclude trials missing required events, no-choice trials, invalid priors, and reaction times outside 0.08–2.00 s.\n6. Bin spikes in 20 ms bins around `stimOn_times`.\n7. Compute absolute filtered wheel velocity with brainbox; use left-camera whisker motion energy with right fallback.\n8. Discretize dynamic behavior using global tertile thresholds stored in metadata.\n9. Remove trials with no spikes from any retained neuron.\n\n## Reproducing and validating\n\n```bash\npython -u /app/convert_data.py /app/sample_data.pkl --sample --show-processing\npython -u Poor performance indicates data formatting issues that need investigation\\n\\n### Consistency requirements\\n\\nYour processing and formatting must **match the reference papers and code** with respect to:\\n- Loading of data\\n- Temporal alignment of different time series streams (neural, inputs, outputs)\\n- Processing of neural, input, and output data streams\\n- Curation of data: filtering of low-quality neurons, trials, sessions, and mice.\\n\\nTo check consistency, you must compare statistics available in the reference paper and your converted dataset. \\n\\nWhenever possible, invent **SANITY CHECKS** that your loading and processing matches the reference paper and code. \\n\\nDiscrepancies are only allowed if required by the Decoder Input and Decoder Output specifications above, or the task of training a neural decoder.\\n\\nCarefully verify your work after every step. When you find mistakes, document and fix them immediately. Be critical of results **after every step of processing**. \\n\\nYou will be assessed on whether the decisions you make on how to load, filter, process, align, reformat, and save the data are reasonable and match the reference paper and code and these instructions. During testing, the reference version of `/app/train_decoder.py` will be run on your converted data. Data statistics and decoder accuracy will be compared to those achieved by human-written conversion code. \\n\\n---\\n\\n## Conversion Workflow\\n\\n**IMPORTANT**: Follow these steps in order. Each step has explicit completion criteria. Do not proceed to the next step until the current step is complete. Use the exact step names below when documenting progress in CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n**STATUS TRACKING**: At the start of each step, update its status to `IN PROGRESS` in CONVERSION_NOTES.md. When complete, update to `COMPLETE`. This helps you and the user track progress.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 0: Setup and Initialization\\n\\n**Goal**: Set up the working environment and create the notes file.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n1. **FIRST**: Create `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md` with the template structure shown at the end of this document\\n2. Verify you can run `python3` and import key packages (numpy, torch)\\n3. If it doesn't exist, STOP and create it now.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 1: Reference Code Exploration\\n\\n**\\u26a0\\ufe0f CONSTRAINT REMINDER**: Only look at code in the `/app/code` directory. Do NOT look outside this project directory.\\n\\n**Goal**: Understand the native data structure\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Identify how data is organized (all files, formats, hierarchies)\\n- Determine available variables and their meanings\\n- Check data dimensions and data types\\n- Look for documentation or README files\\n- Note the data organization and structure\\n- Note dataset size parameters such as the **total number** of subjects (mice), sessions, trials, and neurons\\n\\n**Done when**: You have documented the data structure, file formats, size, and available variables in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 2\\\".\\n\\n**\\u26a0\\ufe0f CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 3, update Step 2 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 3: Reference Text Reading\\n\\n**Goal**: Extract key information from the paper and methods.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Scan the reference papers and methods.txt for important details about the data\\n- Look for and note to file:\\n  - Any information about dataset size (number of neurons, subjects, sessions, trials)\\n  - Fraction of data with different values, e.g. fraction of rewarded outcomes\\n  - Data processing, curation, and filtering\\n  - Variables important to experiments\\n  - Temporal alignment\\n  - Temporal binning\\n- Read the reference paper to find information about expected decoder accuracy.\\n\\n**Done when**: You have documented expected dataset statistics and processing details in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 3\\\".\\n\\n**\\u26a0\\ufe0f CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 4, update Step 3 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 4: Check for Consistency\\n\\n**Goal**: Verify your understanding is consistent across all sources. \\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Compare your understanding of:\\n  - Important functions from exploring the reference code\\n  - Dataset structure from exploring the dataset\\n  - Analysis described in the reference texts\\n- Note and investigate any discrepancies\\n- In particular, look for discrepancies in:\\n  - Experimental and behavioral variables\\n  - Data processing\\n  - Data curation\\n- Iterate until your understanding of the reference code, dataset, and reference texts are consistent\\n\\n**Done when**: You have resolved all discrepancies and documented your final understanding in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 4\\\".\\n\\n**\\u26a0\\ufe0f CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 5, update Step 4 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 5: Mapping Planning\\n\\n**Goal**: Create a detailed plan for mapping source data to target format.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Map source data elements to target format components:\\n  - (Follow Decoder Task section)\\n  - How to discretize continuous outputs (Follow Decoder Task section)\\n  - Which inputs/outputs should be **time-varying** vs **per-trial** (Follow Decoder Task section)\\n  - How does the reference code load and manipulate this data?\\n  - When possible, import or copy code from the reference code in `/app/code` directory. \\n- Consult CONVERSION_NOTES.md under Steps 1-4 and reference materials to determine:\\n  - Temporal binning for spike rates (if applicable)\\n  - Temporal alignment of trials\\n  - Data filtering and curation rules for neurons, trials, and sessions\\n  - Brain regions recorded from\\n- Mapping should be consistent with CONVERSION_NOTES.md under Steps 1-4.\\n- Check for variables indicating valid data periods \\u2014 exclude invalid data\\n- Note all decisions, edge cases, and data quality issues\\n- Plan and document **sanity and consistency checks** based on dataset size information from the reference texts, code, and data\\n\\n**Done when**:\\n- You have a complete mapping document in CONVERSION_NOTES.md specifying every source-to-target variable mapping under \\\"Step 5\\\"\\n- You have documented all decisions under \\\"Step 5\\\"\\n- You have documented sanity and consistency checks under \\\"Step 5\\\"\\n\\n**\\u26a0\\ufe0f CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 6, update Step 5 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 6: Script Development\\n\\n**Goal**: Write the conversion script to `/app/convert_data.py`.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Write all conversion code in the file `/app/convert_data.py`\\n- Script should run as **`python -u /app/convert_data.py <outpicklefile>`**\\n- Include options:\\n  - `--full` (default): Process all sessions\\n  - `--sample`: Process only 2 sessions for testing\\n  - `--show-processing`: Plot visualizations of EVERY processing step for up to 2 sessions. Save plots as `processing_<session_id>.png`.\\n- Reuse code from reference code bases where appropriate\\n- Use the `ONE` API to interface with the data. Do not directly read the data files. \\n- Write efficient code:\\n  - Vectorize loops\\n  - Avoid unnecessary file I/O\\n  - Use parallel processing if beneficial\\n  - Print timing information to find bottlenecks\\n- Plots for `--show-processing` mode should visually convince the user that every step of the conversion is correct.\\n  - There are no temporal misalignments\\n  - Discretization of continuous outputs is correct\\n- Write clear, well-documented functions\\n- Handle missing data appropriately (consult references, use sensible defaults, document)\\n- Validate data shapes and types at each step\\n- Include sanity checks (e.g., trial counts match across arrays)\\n\\n**Done when**: `/app/convert_data.py` exists and runs efficiently without errors.\\n\\n**\\u26a0\\ufe0f DO NOT PROCEED** to Step 7 until `/app/convert_data.py` exists and you have updated Step 6 in CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 7: Sample Conversion and Validation\\n\\n**Goal**: Validate the conversion on a small sample before processing the full dataset.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n1. Run `python -u /app/convert_data.py /app/sample_data.pkl --sample --show-processing 2>&1 | tee /app/conversion_sample_out.txt`\\n  a. Verify the sample data structure matches the specification.\\n  b. Check dimensions are consistent across trials/sessions.\\n  c. Check that no data is missed during conversion. \\n  d. Validate that metadata accurately describes the data.\\n2. Improve efficiency of conversion.\\n  a. Look at and note timing information for the conversion. \\n  b. Estimate how long the full conversion will run. When you do this, make sure that your estimate accounts for differences in lengths/numbers of trials/sessions. \\n  c. If full conversion time estimate is longer than 15 minutes, speed up the code by writing more efficient code (vectorizing loops, removing unnecessary or redundant computations) and/or including parallel processing. \\n3. Run `python -u /app/train_decoder.py /app/sample_data.pkl --verify-only 2>&1 | tee /app/verification_sample_out.txt`.\\n4. Analyze the output file `/app/verification_sample_out.txt`:\\n  a. Review your time estimate from Step 7.\\n2. If estimated time is long (e.g. longer than 15 minutes), optimize bottlenecks first.\\n3. Run `python -u /app/convert_data.py /app/converted_data.pkl --full 2>&1 | tee /app/conversion_full_out.txt`\\n4. As the code runs, update your estimates of how long processing will take. If it is much longer than your previous estimate (> 1.5x), kill the process, optimize bottlenecks, and repeat. \\n5. Run `python -u /app/train_decoder.py /app/converted_data.pkl --verify-only 2>&1 | tee /app/verification_full_out.txt`. \\n6. Check that no data was lost during conversion \\n7. Spot-check a few sessions to verify data integrity\\n8. **Check for consistency** between dataset statistics in `/app/verification_full_out.txt` and the reference texts\\n9. Investigate any inconsistencies, and revise the conversion script until all dataset statistics are consistent\\n\\n**Done when**:\\n- `/app/converted_data.pkl` is created and passes manual inspection\\n- `/app/verification_full_out.txt` is created and passes inspection\\n- **ALL** dataset statistics are consistent with values from reference texts\\n- You have documented statistics and consistency in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 9\\\"\\n\\n**\\u26a0\\ufe0f DO NOT PROCEED** to Step 10 until `/app/converted_data.pkl` and `/app/verification_full_out.txt` files exist and CONVERSION_NOTES.MD Step 9 is filled in.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 10: Critical Review 1\\n\\n**Goal**: Find and fix any errors by performing the following checks. Address each warning by either fixing its cause or verifying it that it is not possible to fix it. Explain why each warning could not be fixed in `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md`. \\n\\n**Check 2: Construct sanity checks**\\n- Develop at least one sanity check each on neural, input, and output data.\\n- These must involve loading in the original data files (NOT through your conversion code).\\n- Construct comparison tests and criteria using `np.allclose()`. \\n- These tests can be spot-checks of the data, e.g. neural activity at trial 5, timepoint 10, neuron 3. \\n- Fix all mismatches/sanity check failures. \\n- Document your sanity checks to `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md`. \\n\\n**Check 3: Reference code comparison**\\n- Compare your code to the reference code and methods. \\n- For each major processing step \\u2014 (a) data loading, (b) neuron/trial filtering, (c) temporal alignment, (d) binning, (e) input construction, (f) output construction \\u2014 identify the corresponding code in your script and in the reference, and compare the logic. \\n- Check whether you use the same variables, filtering, and processing as the reference code. \\n- Fix any mismatches. \\n- Document your comparisons in `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md`. \\n- Explain your reasoning for any differences in `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md`.\\n\\n**Check 4: Key statistics comparison**\\n- Verify that key statistics (number of animals, sessions, trials, neurons, input and output ranges, output distributions) match information available in the reference papers. \\n- Write code to investigate any discrepancies. \\n- Fix any discovered issues. \\n- Document your comparisons in `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md`. \\n\\n**Check 5: Check for edge cases**\\n- Check for off-by-one errors at the beginning/ends of trials, sessions, and subjects, or in definitions of the inputs and outputs. \\n- There may be minor issues in the data that your code must handle. Check that your code robustly handles issues in the original data. \\n\\n**Iteration protocol**: If ANY check above reveals an issue:\\n1. Fix the issue in convert_data.py\\n2. Re-run the affected conversion and validation steps\\n3. Re-run ALL checks in this step (not just the one that failed)\\n4. Document each iteration: what was found, what was fixed, what the re-check showed\\n\\nWrite a report to CONVERSION_NOTES.md describing **every** check you did, to help convince the user that the conversion code works. **Done when**: You have documented your review findings and all issues are resolved in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 10\\\".\\n\\n**\\u26a0\\ufe0f DO NOT PROCEED** to Step 11 until you have checked for consistency between **every** statistic in the reference texts, code, and data and documented in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under Step 10. \\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 11: Full Decoder Training\\n\\n**Goal**: Validate the decoder on the **complete** dataset.\\n\\n**\\u26a0\\ufe0f IMPORTANT**: This step must complete fully. Do not skip or abbreviate. Do not proceed to Step 12 until this step is completely finished.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n1. Run `python -u /app/train_decoder.py /app/converted_data.pkl --plot-samples 2>&1 | tee /app/train_decoder_full_out.txt`. If the GPU does not have sufficient RAM for the network training, use the flag `--cpu` to specify to use the CPU to train. \\n2. **Wait for complete execution** \\u2014 this may take significant time for large datasets\\n3. **Check training**: Verify loss decreases over epochs\\n4. **Check accuracy**: High accuracy is an indicator that data conversion has been done correctly. Accuracy near chance is a sign that there might be issues in temporal alignment of signals, choice of data streams, or filtering or processing of data. Compare accuracy to expectations based on the papers. \\n\\n**Done when**: \\n1. Full decoder training completes (the script finishes running)\\n2. Accuracy results are documented in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 11\\\" with a table of accuracies\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 12: Critical Review 2\\n\\n**Goal**: Find and fix any errors by performing the following checks. Fix issues and re-run affected steps. Iterate until no issues remain. Perform all of the following checks:\\n\\n**Check 1: Accuracy vs chance analysis**\\n- For each output, compare validation accuracy to chance (1/num_classes)\\n- Accuracy below chance indicates a bug, investigate and fix conversion issues to improve this. \\n- Accuracy below 1.5x chance may also indicate a bug, investigate whether changes in conversion logic could improve accuracy. \\n\\n**Check 2: Accuracy comparison to papers**\\n- Find every decoding accuracy reported in the reference papers\\n- Create a table comparing your accuracy to the papers's accuracy for each variable\\n- If your accuracy is lower than the reported accuracy, this may indicate a bug in your conversion that you must fix. \\n- Differences in algorithm/architecture should be relatively small because of the data dimensionality and size. Do not use this as an excuse to dismiss differences, investigate them completely before moving on. \\n\\n**Check 3: Train vs validation gap**\\n- If training accuracy is much higher (>1.5x) than validation accuracy for any output, investigate overfitting or data leakage. \\n\\n**If accuracy is low for an output, try these specific debugging steps:**\\n1. Verify the output values are correct by loading raw data and checking 3 specific trials\\n2. Check temporal alignment \\u2014 plot neural + output for a single trial to verify they're synchronized\\n3. Check whether the output has enough variation (not 99% one class)\\n4. Check that filtering steps for neural activity streams are followed. \\n5. Check that processing of the data matches the reference code and papers. \\n\\n**Iteration protocol**: If ANY check above reveals an issue:\\n1. Fix the issue in convert_data.py\\n2. Re-run the affected conversion and validation steps\\n3. Re-run ALL checks in this step (not just the one that failed)\\n4. Document each iteration: what was found, what was fixed, what the re-check showed\\n\\n**Report all checks and results** to `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md` to convince the user that the conversion and decoding has been done correctly. \\n\\n**Done when**: You have documented your review findings and all issues are resolved in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 12\\\".\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 13: Documentation and Cleanup\\n\\n**Goal**: Finalize documentation and organize files.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Ensure CONVERSION_NOTES.md is complete with all:\\n  - Key decisions and rationale\\n  - Checks for correctness of the conversion\\n  - Validation results and tables\\n  - Any issues found and how they were resolved\\n- Create a user-facing `/app/README.md` summarizing:\\n  - Dataset description\\n  - How to load and use the converted data\\n  - Output format specification\\n  - Key statistics\\n- Move analysis/investigation scripts to a `/app/cache/` folder\\n- Create `/app/cache/README_CACHE.md` documenting cached files\\n\\n**Done when**: README.md exists, CONVERSION_NOTES.md is complete, and directory is clean.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## CONVERSION_NOTES.md Template\\n\\n**Create this file IMMEDIATELY in Step 0.
